title: Concavity conjecture for the generalized inverse hyperbolic sine
statement:
For $x\in(0,1)$ fixed, let $p\mapsto {\rm arcsinh}_p(x)$ denote the generalized inverse hyperbolic sine as a function of $p$. **Concavity conjecture.** The function $p\mapsto {\rm arcsinh}_p(x)$ is strictly concave on $(0,\infty)$. In particular, for all $p>1$ and $x\in(0,1)$,

$$
{\rm arcsinh}_p^2(x)>{\rm arcsinh}_{p-1}(x){\rm arcsinh}_{p+1}(x).
$$

This conjecture is motivated by computer experiments; the asserted strict concavity would imply the displayed Turán-type inequality.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0938

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).
source_name: Árpád Baricz, Barkat Ali Bhayo and Matti Vuorinen, “Turán type inequalities for generalized inverse trigonometric functions”, arXiv:1305.0938 (2013).
